items.headline: OpenAI partners with Hacktron to hunt for system vulnerabilities
items.summary: OpenAI is working with Hacktron to locate vulnerabilities, test third‑party connections and bolster its defenses using frontier AI.
items.why_it_matters: Strengthening security helps protect OpenAI’s services and users.
items.evidence_quote: OpenAI is partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities, test connections with third-party services, and strengthen defenses with frontier AI.

items.headline: OpenAI launches BioBasicsBench benchmark for wet‑lab AI agents
items.summary: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a benchmark of 100 tasks that measures how AI agents interpret raw experimental data and perform everyday wet‑lab work.
items.why_it_matters: The benchmark provides a standard to evaluate AI’s usefulness in scientific research.
items.evidence_quote: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.

items.headline: Concerns over Nvidia H200 chips sold to empty Chinese firm
items.summary: The New York Times reports that New Matrix, listed as approved to receive Nvidia’s H200 AI chips, appears to have no operational offices.
items.why_it_matters: The situation raises questions about vetting of Chinese recipients of advanced AI hardware.
items.evidence_quote: According to The New York Times, New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, "a hollow gray shell …"

items.headline: Hundreds of servers exposing Artex penetration‑testing tool publicly
items.summary: Security researchers discovered many servers hosting the Artex tool openly on the internet, allowing unrestricted access.
items.why_it_matters: Public exposure could enable malicious actors to misuse the hacking tool.
items.evidence_quote: Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.

items.headline: NVIDIA open sources Aerial wireless software for 6G research
items.summary: NVIDIA released its Aerial wireless software as open source, joining other tools to accelerate next‑generation 6G network development.
items.why_it_matters: Open‑source tools help researchers collaborate on future wireless technologies.
items.evidence_quote: NVIDIA open sourced its Aerial wireless software, joining Sionna and a broader suite of open source tools for accelerating next-generation 6G network development.
